explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1185 with the negative answer, which follows from Furstenberg's non-2-intersective difference set. It negates: for all δ > 0 and k ≥ 3 there is m such that for large N, any A ⊆ [1,N] with |A| ≥ δN and B ⊆ [1,N] with |B| ≥ m yields a nontrivial k-AP in A with common difference in B - B. Choosing m before N₀ matches 'm depending only on δ and k'. Truncated subtraction is harmless because d > 0.
